# /rite:review-phase — the phase as a whole

Arguments: `$ARGUMENTS`

Each task was reviewed alone. This looks at what only the whole phase shows: something a later task
broke in an earlier one, tasks that contradict each other, a part of the plan no task delivered.
Review only: never change code, docs or the tasks' work.

## Steps

1. `rite resolve-cycle <cycle> --json`, then `rite phase <cycle> --phase <phase> --json`. The phase is
   required: missing → ask, never pick one. `reviewable` false → the phase is not finished: report
   what is left with its command — `pending` or `blocked` tasks (`/rite:execute-phase`), `unreviewed`
   (`/rite:review-all`), `open_fixes` (`/rite:fix-all`) — and stop.
2. **Delegate** to one fresh `rite:rite-phase-reviewer` agent — never this context. Give it facts
   only: the `rite phase` payload, the payload of `rite context <ID> --json` for the phase's closing
   task (else its last task) — the profile's gates and phase checks —, the repository it works in,
   the CLI invocation, and the instruction "Review this phase per your procedure and return findings
   and gaps in your format." Do not tell it what you think of the work.
3. **Screen.** Keep a finding or a gap only if it carries a runnable evidence command and its output;
   a finding also needs one command that runs on the working tree. Drop one that a fix of the cycle
   already records, naming that fix. Do not re-review, soften or add any of your own; list what you
   dropped, with the reason.
4. **One fix per kept finding**: `rite new-fix --cycle <cycle> --origin <its origin> --title "<title>"
   --severity <critical|high|medium|low> --json`, fill the body sections (Problem, Evidence, Root
   cause, Fix, Files, Verification) — never its frontmatter or the JSON state —, then `rite commit-new
   <FIX> --json`. In Evidence the CLI is `sh "$RITE_HOME/bin/rite"`, never a resolved plugin path.
5. **Gaps become tasks only when the user says so**: they change the scope. Ask once, multi-select, a
   gap whose section states the missing part outright first and marked `(Recommended)`. For each
   chosen: `rite new-task --cycle <cycle> --title "<title>" --type <type> --phase <phase>
   --source-of-truth <link> [--depends-on <IDs>] --json`, fill Scope and verifiable Done criteria,
   `rite set <ID> --files …`, `rite commit-new <ID> --json`. The phase is open again until they are
   done and reviewed. With `--yes`, create none: they stay in the document, to be decided.
6. **Write** `phase-<phase>-review.md` in the cycle folder from
   `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/templates/phase-review.md` — also with nothing found: a review without a
   record was not done — and commit it: `docs(rite): review phase <phase> of <cycle>`. In a local
   cycle it is written and nothing is committed.
7. `rite check --quick --cycle <cycle> --json`.

## Report

The four verdicts, one line each · fixes opened (ID, severity, origin, title) · tasks created, gaps
declined or left to decide · dropped findings and gaps with reasons · the document and its commit
SHA, or "local cycle" · next: `/rite:fix-all`, `/rite:execute-phase <cycle> <phase>`, or "phase clean".

## The CLI

Every state read and every state change goes through it: hand-written bookkeeping drifts.

```sh
sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/rite" <subcommand> [args] --json
```

Find it in that order, never by searching the disk: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/rite`,
`$RITE_HOME/bin/rite`, `rite` on `PATH`; none → ask the user. Below, `rite <sub>` means that
invocation, run inside the repository or with `--root <repo>`; prefer `--json`.

Exit codes: `0` ok · `1` failure or nothing selected (stderr names the rule; no `--force` unless
asked) · `3` no `rite.toml` — stop and tell the user to run `/rite:init`.

Reply in the JSON's `session_language`; empty → the session's language.

## State

The cycle's `progress.json` (meta + tasks) and `fixes.json` are the only state; item files hold prose
and their `id`; the tables in the progress and fixes files are views the CLI renders from the JSON.

- `rite begin <kind> [--cycle C] [--id ID] --json` resolves the cycle, takes the item and returns its
  paths, the config digest and the commit template. Idempotent.
- `rite finish <ID> [--sha S] --json` closes the item from its work commit, runs `check --quick` and
  names the next one. Two commits per item — the work, then the CLI's record (a commit cannot hold its
  own SHA). No work commit, only a document outside git: `--no-repo --reason "…"`, never borrow HEAD.
- Others: `rite mark <ID> blocked|skipped --reason "…" --commit`, `mark-reviewed <ID> [--fixes …]`,
  `mark-stale <FIX> --reason "…"`, `rebind <ID> --sha <commit>` after a squash.
- A fix blocked by the environment adds `--unblocked-by "<command that passes once it is there>"`.
  Partial work: commit what is coherent, then `mark blocked` with the `--reason` naming what is
  missing and the partial SHA — never `close` (not done), never `mark-stale` (the symptom is there).
- A **local cycle** (`"local": true`) writes the same fields and commits nothing, by design; never
  commit its documents yourself.

- Planning fields: `rite set <ID> --files a,b --resources r --depends-on <IDs>`; the cycle's `order`,
  `ticket`, `plan`: `rite set-cycle --cycle C --order <IDs>`. The only fields you write.

Never edit `progress.json` / `fixes.json` (the guard refuses it), never put fields back into an item's
frontmatter, never edit between `<!-- rite:begin … -->` and `<!-- rite:end -->`, never invent an ID.

## Asking the user

Ask only what the repository cannot answer, in one round, with AskUserQuestion (at most 4 questions,
recommended option first). Every question is a context switch; guesses the commands then obey are worse.

With `--yes` in the arguments (or when questions cannot be asked): do not ask. Take the recommended
option of each and list them in the report as `assumed: <question> → <choice>`. Even then, never choose
an option that deletes, moves or overwrites existing files, and never apply retro proposals — write
them down only.

## Evidence

- **Measure, do not read**: a claim counts only if you ran its command here; logs are leads.
- **Every number has a tool**: quote its versioned command beside it.
- **Control before test**: a checker must be seen to fail, Evidence to pass once fixed — a pinned git
  revision or an old log documents, never verifies.
- **Reproduce before fixing** (`rite reproduce <FIX> --json`, `--scratch` if it writes files):
  `REPRODUCED` → fix it · `NOT REPRODUCED` (`why: ok`, output contradicts the Evidence) → *stale*
  (`rite mark-stale`) · else `CANNOT RUN` (other `why`, `cannot_decide`: a `shell_error`,
  `missing_path` or `timed_out`) → an agent or a person, never *stale*. An exit code is not a verdict.
- **Negative results are results**: "X fails, because Y (command, output)".
- **Gates**: `rite gates [--id <ID>] --json`. Red means not done: fix it, or stop and report its
  output.

## Committing

- **Message**: `[commit].style` `conventional` gives `<type>(<scope>): <summary>` (`feat`, `fix`,
  `refactor`, `test`, `docs`, `build`, `chore`), `free` a plain imperative one, in `commit_language`.
  Put your subject in the `subject_template` from `rite begin` and end the body with its `trailers`
  (`Refs: <ID>`, the ticket: what `git log --grep` finds). With `co_author_footer: false`, add no
  `Co-Authored-By` trailer, whatever your attribution asks.
- **Staging**: explicit paths (`git add -- <paths>`), never `git add -A`, never a `never_stage` path.
  In a local cycle, never stage the cycle folder, its profile or its pitfalls file.
- **Never** amend, rebase, force, skip hooks or push by hand; push only when `[commit].push = "on-request"`
  and the user asked in this conversation. With `after-each-item`, `rite finish` and `rite commit-new`
  push: report a failed entry of their `pushed`, never retry it with force. A hook that refuses is reported, never bypassed.
- Every run ends with a commit, except in a local cycle, where a run touching only item files does not.

## Repositories

If `rite begin` gave no `commit.repo_dir`, ignore this section.

An item's work lands in its repository, `commit.repo_dir`: run its commands and git there (`git -C
<repo_dir> …`, a batch's `status` and `stash` too) and read its paths relative to it. One item, one
repository. Rite's documents are never staged there; in a workspace every cycle is local.

## Reporting

**At most 15 lines.** IDs, commands, measured numbers, SHAs, and what the user must decide. Do not
re-tell what the item file already says, and do not paste output that was not decisive.
